title: Principal formal opens, section topologies and canonical comparison data
statement: For the formal spectrum $F=\operatorname{Spf}(R,K)$ [def-per-adic-formal-geometry], define its canonical map to $\operatorname{Spec}R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] by the closed immersions of the defining thickenings. Its principal open $D_F(s)$ is the inverse image of $D(s)$. Define $C_s$ to be the adic completion [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] of $R_s$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] along $KR_s$, with the composite map $R\to R_s\to C_s$. The positive quotient-localization tower has terms $(R/K^{n+1})_s$ and the canonical quotient-localization transitions. The pseudo-discrete topology on a scheme section ring is the initial topology of restrictions to quasi-compact opens endowed with the discrete topology. Formal section rings have the initial topology of the projection maps to the pseudo-discrete quotient sheaf sections. A principal section comparison is a ring isomorphism $\mathcal O_F(D_F(s))\simeq C_s$ which is a homeomorphism for this topology and the $KC_s$-adic topology, and whose composite with restriction of original ring elements is the displayed composite $R\to C_s$. A formal-spectrum morphism inducing a ring map $\varphi:R\to S$ commutes on spaces with the maps to ordinary spectra, is continuous on every section ring for these topologies, and its global-section map extends $\varphi$.
